(Index continues directly from the existing endpoint a(10). ALL ten terms are certified
dual-lineage: Lineage 1 (Claude) = from-scratch fraction-free Gaussian elimination (Bareiss
algorithm) on the exact integer Laplacian minor; Lineage 2 (Codex, independently authored, no
access to Lineage-1 code) = exact modular Gaussian elimination over many primes below 2^31
reconstructed via CRT, with an integer Hadamard bound certifying the reconstruction and a
cross-check against a second Laplacian cofactor mod an unused prime. Both lineages reproduce
every published term a(1)..a(10) exactly and agree digit-for-digit on a(11)..a(20). No index in
this block is single-lineage.)

## 2. Ready-to-paste comment / annotation

a(11)-a(20) computed via Kirchhoff's Matrix-Tree theorem: the n X n king graph's N=n^2-vertex
Laplacian (8-neighbour Chebyshev/king adjacency, D-A) has any cofactor equal to the spanning-tree
count; the cofactor was evaluated as an exact big-integer determinant. Two independently
implemented methods were used — fraction-free Gaussian elimination (Bareiss) and a
multi-modular-determinant-plus-CRT reconstruction with an explicit Hadamard-bound certificate —
and they agree digit-for-digit on all ten new terms, both also reproducing every one of the ten
previously published terms (a(1)..a(10)) exactly. Runtime for a(20) (400 vertices, 399x399
cofactor): a few seconds; peak RSS under 60 MB for the whole run (both lineages).

## 3. Program reference

- Reproducible program (Lineage 1, Bareiss): `research/SCOUT_G/solve.py` (function
  `spanning_trees_king`) / standalone `research/SCOUT_G/king_spanning_trees.py`.
- Independent lineage (Lineage 2, Codex — modular determinant + CRT, own program, no shared
  code): `research/SCOUT_G/RESULT_codex.json` + `research/SCOUT_G/codex_log.txt`
  (dispatched from `research/SCOUT_G/codex_prompt.txt`, which specifies only the problem
  statement and the published gate values).
- Full method, gate table, and dual-lineage certification: `research/SCOUT_G/RESULT.md`.
